claims.answer: Threadlines supplies parent-thread delegation tools: the current agent starts named child threads and receives their final replies, with parent/child relationships owned by the product. Agents can start threads is gated off/ask/auto by user settings. Provider readiness, plan billing and access checks apply before a child can run. thread_send provides follow-up messages to child threads; parent reports arrive asynchronously after the calling turn. With reportBack true, each child final reply returns as a message and wakes the parent, including later self-started child turns. The caller does not block or poll.

sources.title: Threadlines readme
sources.locator: Installation; Supported agents; Configuration; Support development
sources.finding: Threadlines publishes signed macOS/Windows desktop apps and an unsigned Linux AppImage, plus a server CLI and self-hosted Docker service usable from browsers. It drives installed coding agents on the users accounts and is explicitly free/open source.

sources.title: Threadlines docs/providers/claude.md
sources.locator: Claude sign-in; managed SDK session; environment credentials
sources.finding: The Claude Code integration uses a managed SDK session and claude auth login, supports a native saved sign-in and documented API/token environment routes, and distinguishes those credential modes.

sources.title: Threadlines docs/providers/codex.md
sources.locator: Codex sign-in; ChatGPT workspace; model-provider gateway
sources.finding: The Codex integration uses its own saved sign-in, can select a ChatGPT workspace on supported Codex versions, and can use a configured gateway. Gateway and account modes are not treated as additional coding harnesses.

sources.title: Threadlines docs/providers/pi.md
sources.finding: The Pi guide describes native provider sign-in and API-key environment routes. It explicitly warns that Claude Pro/Max used through Pi bills extra usage rather than included plan usage.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/CursorDriver.ts
sources.finding: The exact driver declares Cursor Agent runtime cursor-agent acp and applies the ACP descriptor.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/OpenCodeDriver.ts
sources.finding: The named OpenCode driver manages the OpenCode coding runtime rather than inferring agent support from an API provider name.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/desktop/package.json
sources.locator: main, electron runtime dependency and electron build scripts
sources.finding: The desktop application package uses Electron.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/server/src/mcp/threadTools.ts
sources.finding: The product supplies tools to start parallel child threads, list them and send follow-up messages. Each child gets a self-contained prompt, its own agent session, and by default a worktree off the current commit; final replies report back to the parent when reportBack is true.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/server/src/orchestration/childThreadAgents.ts
sources.finding: Agent-started child threads are gated by provider readiness, billing mode and plan-mode access. The inspected code rejects per-use API-key providers for automatic child starts, and a child cannot gain more access than its parent.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/server/src/mcp/scheduleTools.ts
sources.finding: Scheduled tasks have manual/once/hourly/daily/weekdays/weekly/custom-cron cadences and create a new thread or follow up in the same thread. They run only while Threadlines is running on that computer and get one catch-up run after missed sleep/off time. The setting can ask approval or apply automatically.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/web/src/components/scheduled/ScheduledTaskForm.tsx
sources.locator: ScheduledTaskForm rendered cadence and agent/workspace controls
sources.finding: The product renders a Scheduled task form, connecting the source-defined schedule mechanism to an accessible interface.

sources.title: Threadlines docs/telemetry.md
sources.locator: Opening default statement; What We Collect/Do Not Collect; Configuration
sources.finding: Official builds enable usage analytics by default and offer a Settings opt-out. Events go to PostHog; the policy separates operational metadata from code, prompts, credentials and terminal content, with a documented scrubbed startup-failure-output exception.

sources.title: Threadlines apps/server/src/telemetry/Layers/AnalyticsService.ts
sources.locator: TelemetryEnvConfig; isTelemetryEnabled; applyEnabled; outgoing HTTP batch
sources.finding: The PostHog sender reads usageAnalyticsEnabled and environment overrides, reacts to setting changes, clears buffered collection when disabled and rechecks disk consent before a batch. A bundled key and effective enabled state are required.
